humanities_role_explanation: The pipeline translates classical Islamic religious texts (Qur'an, Hadith, Tafseer, Jurisprudence), which is a general machine translation task applied to humanities content rather than an evaluation of disciplinary humanities reasoning.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: The translation and back-translation evaluation is entirely text-to-text, although an auxiliary multimodal OCR step using GPT-4o for processing image-based PDF pages is described.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Automated machine translation of classical Arabic scholarly texts into English, along with OCR-based document transcription and automated correction using RAG.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: The evaluation focuses exclusively on translating and processing Islamic scholarly literature from the Al-Shamela library.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Evaluates OpenAI's gpt-4o-mini and Anthropic's Claude 3 Haiku (specifically claude-3-haiku-20240307).

quantitative_metrics.note: Uses cosine similarity of sentence embeddings to measure semantic equivalence between original and back-translated text.

summary: The paper presents an automated pipeline using LLMs to translate a massive corpus of classical Islamic literature (over 250,000 pages) from the Al-Shamela library from Arabic to English. The authors use a back-translation validation framework, applying vector embedding cosine similarity to assess the semantic fidelity of translations produced by GPT-4o-mini and Claude 3 Haiku.
key_findings: Both evaluated LLMs demonstrate strong translation fidelity, with 71% of the OpenAI back-translation results and 86% of the Anthropic back-translation results achieving acceptable cosine similarity scores of 0.7 or higher.
facets_explanation: The reference texts are the original classical Arabic pages lifted directly from the digital Al-Shamela Library database. For automated evaluation, the back-translated Arabic text is compared to this single original Arabic source page using cosine similarity of vector embeddings. For manual human-in-the-loop validation, translation corrections are treated as noise/disagreements to be resolved, requiring a consensus of at least two separate reviewers to be accepted.
results_explanation: The paper measures translation fidelity by back-translating English text back to Arabic and computing embedding cosine similarity, reporting that '86% of the Anthropic model results' (using claude-3-haiku-20240307) achieved 'cosine similarity scores >= 0.7' compared to '71% of the OpenAI model results' (using gpt-4o-mini). No numerical human baseline or format/difficulty gap comparisons are provided. While language bias is discussed, the authors explicitly state that the tested commercial LLMs 'did not display detectable language bias between Arabic and English'.
